The O3 framework lazy-loads a React component by wrapping a dynamic `import()` inside a single-spa lifecycle factory. The lifecycle is created when the module is defined, but the component module is only fetched when single-spa or the routes loader first calls the lifecycle.

**Implementation**

1. **`getAsyncLifecycle`** (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/getLifecycle.ts:52-57`) takes a `lazy` function that returns `import('./x.component')` and the decorator options. It returns `() => lazy().then(({ default: Component }) => getLifecycle(Component, options))`. Nothing is imported until that returned function runs.
2. **`getLifecycle`** (same file, lines 26-32) wraps the component with `openmrsComponentDecorator` and passes it to `singleSpaReact`, which produces the bootstrap/mount/unmount object.
3. **`getSyncLifecycle`** (same file, lines 77-79) is the eager variant for components that are already imported. `getAsyncExtensionLifecycle` (line 84) is a deprecated alias of `getAsyncLifecycle`.
4. **Routes loader** (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-routes/src/loaders/load-lifecycles.ts:35-58`): `loadLifeCycles(routesAppName, fullComponentName)` resolves the app name (supporting `app#export` syntax), calls `importDynamic` on the app module, runs its `startupApp()` once via `initializeApp` (lines 86-109), and then calls the named export. The export is the function returned by `getAsyncLifecycle`, so the component chunk loads at this point.
5. **Callers:** extensions and modals in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-routes/src/loaders/components.ts:58` and `:102` set `load: () => loadLifeCycles(appName, extension.component)`. Pages in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-routes/src/loaders/pages.ts:238` do the same. Workspaces in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-styleguide/src/workspaces2/active-workspace-window.component.tsx:71` also call it.

**Usage example:** `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-devtools-app/src/index.ts:10` has `export const devtools = getAsyncLifecycle(() => import('./devtools/devtools.component'), options);`. The other apps follow the same pattern (for example `esm-help-menu-app/src/index.ts:13`).

**Documentation**

- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/getAsyncLifecycle.md:1-52` describes the lazy behavior and includes the example above.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/variables/getAsyncExtensionLifecycle.md` covers the deprecated alias.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/getSyncLifecycle.md` contrasts the eager variant.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/renderExtension.md:10` mentions lazy-loaded components from any frontend module.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/API.md:129` links to the function docs.

I did not read `esm-dynamic-loading`'s `importDynamic` or the extension registration code in `esm-extensions`, so I have not verified how those resolve the module. I also did not read the `components.ts` and `pages.ts` call sites in full.
